text:
sam: quick FYI — sandbox replay of short-chat workload shows host-side CPU dominated by tokenization + small grpc writes. rough split: tokenize ~45%, writev ~25%, kvcache ~8%

emma: can you paste the sample stack / top spots?

sam: here's a condensed sample from pprof:
```
  45.1%  host_ingress  tokenizer::run
  25.3%  host_ingress  grpc::writev_small
   8.2%  host_ingress  kvcache::lookup_remote
   5.6%  host_ingress  http::serialize_frames
```

diego: interesting — tokenize is killing us. Where's the tokenization happening? gateway or host?

sam: gateway does optimistic pretokenize for some clients, but we still run host-side sanitize+re-parse in stream fallback path. found a codepath: gateway sets X-Pretokenized, but host ignores for streaming attachments for safety.

emma: we can make that header authoritative for internal tenants. avoid re-tokenize for internal-only flows. low-risk.

harriet: small grpc writes look like a storm of 128-512 byte buffers. why is writev not coalescing?

sam: our batching window is 1ms in this binary. profiler shows lots of sys_write calls — each small write triggers a syscall.

diego: can we increase window? previously tried 5ms and saw fewer syscalls but latency increased for 1-2 token requests. maybe do adaptive windowing.

emma: proposal: adaptive coalesce: if writev_syscalls/sec > threshold for worker, temporarily increase window to 5-8ms for N ms. revert when rate drops. add metrics to track coalesce_enabled and syscalls_per_sec.

harriet: that sounds reasonable. what's the threshold? 500 syscalls/sec/worker? need tuning.

sam: i'll run microbench with thresholds [200,500,1000] and return numbers.

diego: on kvcache: 8% is small but getting repeated prefix lookups. for tiny requests the overhead is disproportionately high. suggest a per-worker hot-prefix memo with 1024 entries TTL 10s. cheap mem + avoids remote kvcalls.

emma: agree but we must evict aggressively on memory pressure. feature flag gated.

sam: another kernel-selector note: after the kernel switch last week, some nodes picked kernels that optimize token-decode latency but skip merged writev coalesce path. need kernel policy to include a flag for "host-batching-friendly" kernels.

diego: kernel selector currently scores latency and flops. we can add a host-syscall_penalty metric derived from ingress flame snapshots. classifier uses recent seq-length histogram (p10/p50/p95) to bias selection.

emma: good. also add an offline sim: for each kernel candidate, run a short preflight with synthetic short-requests and measure writev_syscalls/second. store profile.

harriet: PR tasks summary:
- gate to respect X-Pretokenized for internal tenants (sam)
- adaptive grpc writev coalesce detector + metrics (emma)
- per-worker hot-prefix memo for kvcache (diego)
- kernel-selector policy: include host-syscall_penalty and seq-hist classifier (emma + diego)

sam: timeline: i'll push pretokenize gate + test harness today. want canary tomorrow.

emma: i'll open detector PR with metrics and canary flag. include dashboard panels: writev_rate, coalesce_active, p50_latency_change.

diego: implementing hot-prefix memo, feature-flagged. will run mem-profiling and set default entries to 512 if memory spike.

emma: kernel policy changes need a short design doc. i'll draft and tag maya for final decision (kernel-owner).

harriet: perf-bot: remind to attach post-change flamegraphs to PR and assert tokenize% drops >= 25% for short workload.

perf-bot: note: Canary slot 3 available. Recommend staging for sampler and canary run after tests pass.

sam: thanks. i'll attach pprof links and the replay harness to the PR. ping me for replay credentials. :thumbsup:
